newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian regulators probe TNT options trading.
newsitem.headline: Australian regulators probe TNT options trading.

text.p: Australian regulators said Thursday they were investigating share trading in TNT Ltd that occurred just before the transport company received a friendly $1.6 billion takeover bid from the Dutch group Koninklijke PTT Nederland.

The Australian Stock Exchange, which first took notice of trading in TNT options last week, said it regarded the matter very seriously and had asked the Australian Securities Commission to begin a formal investigation.

"ASX surveillance has been investigating what it regards as unusual on-market trade in TNT Ltd options," an ASX spokesman said. "The trades took place in the period immediately before the formal announcement to the market of the takeover offer for the company," he said.
Regulatory sources told Reuters they could identify the brokers involved in the options trading that is now under scrutiny, and their clients.
Broker Macquarie Equities told Reuters that it was involved in TNT options trading and had been asked by the ASX to provide information about recent transactions.
"We are very relaxed about it and believe there is nothing untoward," said Macquarie Equities managing director Warwick Evans.

David Poole, an executive director of Macquarie Corporate Finance, which is advising TNT on the takeover bid, said he was not aware of the trading activities of Macquarie Equities. The two divisions are units of the listed Macquarie Bank Ltd.
TNT remained one of the heaviest traded stocks on the Australian market on Thursday as long-suffering shareholders accepted prices that have not been seen this decade.

Brokers said some TNT investors were taking advantage of KPN's generous A$2.45 per share cash offer to bail out. The offer by the Dutch post and telecoms company was 50 percent higher than TNT's share price before the bid was announced.
About 2 percent of TNT's issued ordinary capital, or 11.2 million shares, changed hands on Thursday with the stock closing two cents lower at A$2.42.
